item.title: 13. Matrix Factorizations
item.description:
Factorizations (LU, QR, Cholesky, spectral) turn matrix operations into simpler steps and are the backbone of numerical linear algebra and solvers.

LU and PLU decomposition

If $A$ can be reduced to row echelon form without row swaps:

$$ A = LU $$

  • $L$: Unit lower triangular (multipliers from elimination).
  • $U$: Upper triangular (echelon form).

General case (with row swaps): $PA = LU$ where $P$ is a permutation matrix.

Solving $A\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{b}$: (1) Solve $L\mathbf{y} = P\mathbf{b}$ (forward substitution); (2) Solve $U\mathbf{x} = \mathbf{y}$ (back substitution). Once $L,U$ (and $P$) are computed, many right-hand sides are cheap.
